name: Sauerbraten (German Braised Beef Pot Roast)
method: slow braise (oven, 300F) - adaptable to slow cooker
unmapped: rump roast (board tracks chuck-roast/sirloin/ribeye, not rump roast - closest home is chuck-roast)
golden raisins (board tracks raisins, not golden specifically - minor)
lard (recipe offers vegetable-oil alternative which IS on board)
why: Verified published nutrition (READ from page): 590 cal, 29.6g carb, 60.9g protein per serving - squarely in the 400-650 cal / <=35g carb band with elite protein-to-calorie ratio. German cuisine is absent from the catalog (which skews American/Tex-Mex), and there is no existing sauerbraten. Structurally low-carb: beef + aromatics in a sweet-sour braise, no rice/pasta/potato base; the only carb sources are a little sugar, raisins, and 8 crushed gingersnaps for the gravy. A whole-muscle beef braise scales cleanly to 14 servings with weigh-and-divide. Good pricer-lane specimen: juniper berries are genuinely off the board and rump roast needs a cut mapping (chuck-roast is the sane home).
